what: Deep-network Laplacian per call on JAX with CUDA: omnibias planned default (forward: differentiate none; value-and-gradient: differentiate params, split stream layout) against folx (dense and sparse), jax.experimental.jet, nested autodiff and the dense Hessian trace, 40 cells of the per-call grid
hardware: one exclusive NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB per round, JAX 0.10.2, one fresh process per round, 4 rounds per precision
protocol: f64: 4/f32h: 4/f32t: 4 fresh-process rounds of the 40-cell per-call grid; the omnibias program and every baseline are timed in the same process of a round (host-timed call: median of repeated blocks; device: mean of 32 back-to-back calls with one synchronisation, a CUDA-graph replay on PyTorch); ratio = baseline time / omnibias time, median over rounds, 95 % hierarchical bootstrap interval over rounds; the forward rows of the two-hidden-layer float64 cells come from the rounds run with layout="split", which is what "auto" selects for them (the rounds of the default layout ran on one snapshot of the code and the split rounds on the next, which differs in the CPU planner prior and in the PyTorch streams only, not in a JAX accelerator code path)
